obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 11, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Freeze the funds and economic resources of persons designated under the Belarus sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Belarus sanctions, no one may deal with funds or economic resources that a designated person owns, holds or controls, directly or through an entity it owns or controls, when they know or have reasonable cause to suspect it. Dealing covers using, moving, transferring or giving access to funds and any change, portfolio management included, that would let them be used, as well as exchanging or pledging economic resources for funds, goods or services. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Belarus sanctions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), regs. 12 to 15, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Belarus sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Belarus sanctions, no one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, provide funds or economic resources directly or indirectly to a designated person, or to anyone for its benefit; economic resources given to the designated person itself are caught only where the giver also knows or suspects that it would likely exchange them for, or use them to obtain, funds, goods or services. Provision to an entity the designated person owns or controls counts as indirect, and a designated person benefits only where it gains, or can gain, a significant financial benefit, such as the discharge of a debt it owes in whole or in part. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not deal in the restricted transferable securities and money-market instruments of the Belarusian state and Belarusian entities
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 15A, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Do not deal in the restricted transferable securities and money-market instruments of the Belarusian state and Belarusian entities

summaries.en: No one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, deal directly or indirectly in transferable securities or money-market instruments issued by a relevant person, meaning Belarus, a Belarusian authority, an entity wholly owned by either, a credit or financial institution majority owned by either and certain entities linked to such an institution: those maturing after more than 90 days issued in the window opened by the 2021 amending regulations, and any issued after the 2022 amending regulations came into force. The same holds for instruments issued since 2022 by other persons connected with Belarus, other than those then domiciled elsewhere and their branches and subsidiaries, by entities they majority own and by those acting for them; dealing includes buying, selling, providing investment services and helping with an issue. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Grant no restricted loan or credit to the Belarusian state, Belarusian entities or entities linked to them
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 15B, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Grant no restricted loan or credit to the Belarusian state, Belarusian entities or entities linked to them

summaries.en: No one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, grant a relevant loan or enter into an arrangement to grant one, directly or indirectly. Relevant loans are any loan or credit first granted to a relevant person under the regulations after the 2022 amending regulations came into force, loans of more than 90 days granted to such a person in the earlier window opened by the 2021 amending regulations, and loans of more than 30 days granted since 2022 to other entities connected with Belarus, other than those then domiciled elsewhere or majority owned by such an entity, or to entities they majority own. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Provide no financial services for the reserve and asset management of the National Bank or the Ministry of Finance of Belarus
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 15CA, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Provide no financial services for the reserve and asset management of the National Bank or the Ministry of Finance of Belarus

summaries.en: No one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, provide financial services for the management of foreign exchange reserves and assets to the National Bank of Belarus, the Ministry of Finance of Belarus, an entity either of them owns or controls directly or indirectly, or anyone acting for either of them. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep to the conditions of a Treasury licence relied on under the Belarus sanctions and apply for one truthfully
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 35, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep to the conditions of a Treasury licence relied on under the Belarus sanctions and apply for one truthfully

summaries.en: Under the Belarus sanctions, anyone who knowingly or recklessly gives materially false information, or a document that is not what it claims to be, to obtain a Treasury licence for themselves or another commits an offence. So does anyone who purports to act under a Treasury licence and fails to meet any of its conditions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report designated persons, held assets and suspected breaches under the Belarus sanctions to the Treasury
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), reg. 38, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Report designated persons, held assets and suspected breaches under the Belarus sanctions to the Treasury

summaries.en: Under the Belarus sanctions, a relevant firm, which includes any firm with a Part 4A permission, must inform the Treasury as soon as practicable when information that reached it in the course of its business gives it knowledge or reasonable cause to suspect that a person is designated or has breached the finance prohibitions or committed a finance licensing offence, giving the grounds and the identifying details it holds and, for a customer known or suspected to be designated, the funds and economic resources it held for that customer when it first knew or suspected it. Since 5 December 2024 anyone who knows or suspects that it holds funds or economic resources of a designated person also reports their nature and amount as held on 30 September by 30 November each year, and reports in the following year once it no longer holds them. A firm with a Part 4A permission informs the Treasury without delay when it credits a frozen account or transfers funds from one under the exceptions the regulations allow.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Syria (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/792), reg. 19, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Do not trade in or broker bonds of the former Assad regime with Syrian credit or financial institutions

summaries.en: No one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, sell to or buy from a Syrian credit or financial institution, someone acting for one or an entity one owns or controls, directly or indirectly, bonds issued or guaranteed by the Assad regime between 19 January 2012 and 8 December 2024, or provide brokering services to such a person for those bonds. Nor may anyone provide brokering, advertising or any other service knowing or suspecting that it helps such a person buy or sell bonds the Assad regime issued or guaranteed; a Syrian credit or financial institution is one domiciled in Syria, or its branch or subsidiary anywhere. A breach is an offence, and only the exception for national security and the prevention of serious crime applies.

titles.en: Keep to the conditions of a Treasury licence relied on under the Myanmar sanctions and apply for one truthfully

summaries.en: Under the Myanmar sanctions, anyone who knowingly or recklessly gives materially false information, or a document that is not what it claims to be, to obtain a Treasury licence for themselves or another commits an offence. titles.en: Report designated persons, held assets and suspected breaches under the Myanmar sanctions to the Treasury

summaries.en: Under the Myanmar sanctions, a relevant firm, which includes any firm with a Part 4A permission, must inform the Treasury as soon as practicable when information that reached it in the course of its business gives it knowledge or reasonable cause to suspect that a person is designated or has breached the finance prohibitions or committed a finance licensing offence, giving the grounds and the identifying details it holds and, for a customer known or suspected to be designated, the funds and economic resources it held for that customer when it first knew or suspected it. Since 5 December 2024 anyone who knows or suspects that it holds funds or economic resources of a designated person also reports their nature and amount as held on 30 September by 30 November each year, and reports in the following year once it no longer holds them. A firm with a Part 4A permission informs the Treasury without delay when it credits a frozen account or transfers funds from one under the exceptions the regulations allow.

titles.en: Freeze the funds and economic resources of persons designated under the chemical weapons sanctions

summaries.en: Under the chemical weapons sanctions, no one may deal with funds or economic resources that a designated person owns, holds or controls, directly or through an entity it owns or controls, when they know or have reasonable cause to suspect it. Dealing covers using, moving, transferring or giving access to funds and any change, portfolio management included, that would let them be used, as well as exchanging or pledging economic resources for funds, goods or services. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

titles.en: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the chemical weapons sanctions

summaries.en: Under the chemical weapons sanctions, no one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, provide funds or economic resources directly or indirectly to a designated person, or to anyone for its benefit; economic resources given to the designated person itself are caught only where the giver also knows or suspects that it would likely exchange them for, or use them to obtain, funds, goods or services. Provision to an entity the designated person owns or controls counts as indirect, and a designated person benefits only where it gains, or can gain, a significant financial benefit, such as the discharge of a debt it owes in whole or in part. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Open no account, correspondent relationship or joint venture with an Iranian bank and set up no office in Iran
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Iran (Sanctions) (Nuclear) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/461), reg. 17B, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Open no account, correspondent relationship or joint venture with an Iranian bank and set up no office in Iran

summaries.en: A UK credit or financial institution, which includes any firm with a Part 4A permission, must not open a bank account with, or start a correspondent banking relationship or joint venture with, a credit or financial institution domiciled in Iran, its branch or subsidiary anywhere, or one owned or controlled by a person domiciled in Iran, when it knows or has reasonable cause to suspect it, and must not open a representative office, branch or subsidiary in Iran. No one may set up such an Iranian institution's office, branch or subsidiary in the United Kingdom, arrange it or authorise new business by one not authorised before 8 September 2026, and such an institution may not acquire or extend a participation, or any ownership stake, in a United Kingdom credit or financial institution. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

titles.en: Do not trade in or broker Iranian state bonds issued after 8 September 2026

summaries.en: No one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, sell to or buy from the Government of Iran, an Iranian credit or financial institution, someone acting for either or an entity either owns or controls, directly or indirectly, bonds that the Government of Iran issued or guaranteed after 8 September 2026, or provide brokering services to such a person for those bonds. Nor may anyone provide brokering, advertising or any other service knowing or suspecting that it helps such a person issue bonds the Government of Iran issues or guarantees. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

titles.en: Report designated persons, held assets and suspected breaches under the Sudan sanctions to the Treasury

summaries.en: Under the Sudan sanctions, a relevant firm, which includes any firm with a Part 4A permission, must inform the Treasury as soon as practicable when information that reached it in the course of its business gives it knowledge or reasonable cause to suspect that a person is designated or has breached the finance prohibitions or committed a finance licensing offence, giving the grounds and the identifying details it holds and, for a customer known or suspected to be designated, the funds and economic resources it held for that customer when it first knew or suspected it. Since 5 December 2024 anyone who knows or suspects that it holds funds or economic resources of a designated person also reports their nature and amount as held on 30 September by 30 November each year, and reports in the following year once it no longer holds them. A firm with a Part 4A permission informs the Treasury without delay when it credits a frozen account or transfers funds from one under the exceptions the regulations allow.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Yemen (Sanctions) (EU Exit) (No. 2) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020/1278), reg. 12, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Freeze the funds and economic resources of persons designated under the Yemen sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Yemen sanctions, no one may deal with funds or economic resources that a designated person owns, holds or controls, directly or through an entity it owns or controls, when they know or have reasonable cause to suspect it. Dealing covers using, moving, transferring or giving access to funds and any change, portfolio management included, that would let them be used, as well as exchanging or pledging economic resources for funds, goods or services. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Yemen sanctions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Yemen (Sanctions) (EU Exit) (No. 2) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020/1278), regs. 13 to 16, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Yemen sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Yemen sanctions, no one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, provide funds or economic resources directly or indirectly to a designated person, or to anyone for its benefit; economic resources given to the designated person itself are caught only where the giver also knows or suspects that it would likely exchange them for, or use them to obtain, funds, goods or services. Provision to an entity the designated person owns or controls counts as indirect, and a designated person benefits only where it gains, or can gain, a significant financial benefit, such as the discharge of a debt it owes in whole or in part. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

Since 5 December 2024 anyone who knows or suspects that it holds funds or economic resources of a designated person also reports their nature and amount as held on 30 September by 30 November each year, and reports in the following year once it no longer holds them. A firm with a Part 4A permission informs the Treasury without delay when it credits a frozen account or transfers funds from one under the exceptions the regulations allow.

titles.en: Freeze the funds and economic resources of persons designated under the Haiti sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Haiti sanctions, no one may deal with funds or economic resources that a designated person owns, holds or controls, directly or through an entity it owns or controls, when they know or have reasonable cause to suspect it. Dealing covers using, moving, transferring or giving access to funds and any change, portfolio management included, that would let them be used, as well as exchanging or pledging economic resources for funds, goods or services. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Haiti sanctions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Haiti (Sanctions) Regulations 2022 (S.I. 2022/1281), regs. 9 to 12, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Make no funds or economic resources available to or for the benefit of persons designated under the Haiti sanctions

summaries.en: Under the Haiti sanctions, no one may, knowing or with reasonable cause to suspect it, provide funds or economic resources directly or indirectly to a designated person, or to anyone for its benefit; economic resources given to the designated person itself are caught only where the giver also knows or suspects that it would likely exchange them for, or use them to obtain, funds, goods or services. Provision to an entity the designated person owns or controls counts as indirect, and a designated person benefits only where it gains, or can gain, a significant financial benefit, such as the discharge of a debt it owes in whole or in part. A breach is a criminal offence unless an exception or a licence under the regulations covers it.

titles.en: Keep to the conditions of a Treasury licence relied on under the Haiti sanctions and apply for one truthfully

summaries.en: Under the Haiti sanctions, anyone who knowingly or recklessly gives materially false information, or a document that is not what it claims to be, to obtain a Treasury licence for themselves or another commits an offence. So does anyone who purports to act under a Treasury licence and fails to meet any of its conditions.

titles.en: Hold no commodity derivative position above a position limit the FCA has set by direction

summaries.en: No person, wherever it is, may hold a position in a commodity derivative that exceeds a position limit the FCA has established by direction under regulation 16. The limits are published as the FCA thinks fit, and where they apply they take the place of the limits set by virtue of regulation 15A.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework's due diligence procedures to cryptoasset users
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), reg. 4(1), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Apply the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework's due diligence procedures to cryptoasset users

summaries.en: A UK reporting cryptoasset service provider must apply the due diligence procedures in Section III of the rules of the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, and set up and keep arrangements designed to apply them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the due diligence records for five years after the calendar year they relate to
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), reg. 4(2) to (4), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep the due diligence records for five years after the calendar year they relate to

summaries.en: A UK reporting cryptoasset service provider must record the steps it took to apply the due diligence procedures and the information it collected in doing so. It keeps each record for five years, counted from the day after the close of the calendar year in which the information was collected, generated or relied on.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report each calendar year's user and transaction information to HMRC by 31 May
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), regs. 6 and 7, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Report each calendar year's user and transaction information to HMRC by 31 May

summaries.en: For each calendar year a UK reporting cryptoasset service provider must report to HMRC, by 31 May of the following year, the information that Section II(A) to (F) of the framework's rules requires; a provider that reports only because of a United Kingdom branch reports the transactions carried out through that branch. The report goes through HMRC's electronic report system in the form and manner HMRC directs, and a report made any other way counts as not made.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell reportable users and persons that their information goes to HMRC and may be passed abroad
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), reg. 8, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Tell reportable users and persons that their information goes to HMRC and may be passed abroad

summaries.en: A UK reporting cryptoasset service provider whose report will include information on a reportable user or reportable person must tell that user or person that the information will be reported to HMRC and may be passed to another jurisdiction's competent authority under the framework. It does so by 31 January after the first calendar year for which it must report that person's information.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with HMRC as a reporting cryptoasset service provider
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), reg. 10, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Register with HMRC as a reporting cryptoasset service provider

summaries.en: A UK reporting cryptoasset service provider, and a provider that has notified HMRC under Section I(H) of the framework's rules, must register with HMRC by notice in the form and with the information HMRC directs. The deadline is the later of 31 May 2027 and 31 January after the first calendar year in which it became such a provider or had to give that notification.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Carry on consumer buy-to-let mortgage business only once entered on the register
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Mortgage Credit Directive Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/910), art. 7, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Carry on consumer buy-to-let mortgage business only once entered on the register

summaries.en: A firm whose Part 4A permission covers an activity of a kind that article 7 names from the Regulated Activities Order (articles 25A, 36A, 53A, 53DA, 60B and 61), which include arranging and advising on regulated mortgage contracts, credit broking and regulated credit agreements, may not act as creditor, credit intermediary or adviser on consumer buy-to-let mortgage contracts unless the firm is on the register of consumer buy-to-let mortgage firms. A consumer buy-to-let mortgage is a buy-to-let mortgage the borrower takes out not wholly or mainly for a business it runs or intends to run.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the requirements of Schedule 2 in consumer buy-to-let mortgage business
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Mortgage Credit Directive Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/910), art. 18(1)(a), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Meet the requirements of Schedule 2 in consumer buy-to-let mortgage business

summaries.en: A firm on the consumer buy-to-let register must meet the requirements Schedule 2 sets for its consumer buy-to-let mortgage business, which cover, among other things, conduct towards consumers, the knowledge and competence of staff, pre-contractual information and explanations, the disclosure and checking of borrower information, foreign currency loans, early repayment and changes in the borrowing rate. Part 3 does not apply to agreements entered into before 21 March 2016.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the evidence of compliance with Schedule 2 for as long as the mortgage runs
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Mortgage Credit Directive Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/910), art. 18(1)(b), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep the evidence of compliance with Schedule 2 for as long as the mortgage runs

summaries.en: A firm on the consumer buy-to-let register must keep the information that shows whether it has met the requirements of Schedule 2, in a form that can be retrieved and read, for as long as any sum stays owed or any mortgage or charge stays in place under the contract it concerns.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the FCA the consumer buy-to-let information it directs and deal with it openly
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Mortgage Credit Directive Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/910), art. 18(1)(c) and (d) and (2), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give the FCA the consumer buy-to-let information it directs and deal with it openly

summaries.en: A firm on the consumer buy-to-let register must give the FCA the information the FCA directs about that business and about how it meets Schedule 2, at the times, in the manner and verified as the FCA directs. In all its dealings with the FCA it must be open and co-operate.
